items.label: A
items.critique: Generic world-news rumours (trade routes, brazen Ogres, strange noises in alleys) in full, calm sentences with 'Be careful if you plan on traveling.' This is the campaign's townsfolk filler.

items.label: B
items.critique: Three one-liners, unrelated and a bit absurd ('You'll become a drunkard before you know it', 'Beware of the rising undead'). This is classic Westwood throwaway banter.

items.label: C
items.critique: 'Maybe we shouldn't have built so close to the ogre village' and 'Well good luck to ya' are Westwood's dry, self-mocking townsfolk humour.

items.label: D
items.critique: Each line is a quest pointer with a named giver, the problem and where to go ('offering a reward', 'out by their den', 'buy him a drink'). Functional and dense with names.

items.label: E
items.critique: Three quest hooks in a row, each ending in '[Person] wants...!' with exclamation marks. Nothing here is mere colour.

items.label: F
items.critique: Wolves taking half the sheep, a bounty, Urchins from the barrow stealing an heirloom and bandits at the watchtower: a menu of side quests voiced as gossip.

items.label: G
items.critique: A directional 'head over to [Place]' and 'beyond the grand statue', plus a city-machinery complaint about the Chief Engineer. Bland and plain, with an unforced Westwood flavour.

items.label: H
items.critique: 'That unfortunate lad will wish he'd never even heard of the old goat' and 'I don't know who spreads these insane rumors' carry sly, self-aware humour and longer sentences.

items.label: I
items.critique: 'Mawweeds ate them, she says! Plants!' is a good beat, but all three lines are quest pointers with names, places and exclamations.

items.label: J
items.critique: A missing novice, a pony-sized wolf, a stolen tithe chest, each line naming who wants what. Same structure and punctuation as D/E/F/I.

tells: New rumours are all quest signposts: every line names a quest-giver, the trouble and the place, often ending with '[Person] wants...' or 'offering a reward'. Westwood's rumours are mostly colour, general world news or jokes, with at most a loose hint.
Name density: new lines pack two or three masked names each. Westwood's use few and favour generic nouns ('the ogres', 'bandits', 'merchants').
Punctuation: the new lines end almost every sentence in '!'. Westwood's townsfolk speak in calmer statements with periods, and the humour is dry and self-deprecating rather than exclaimed.
Westwood's three lines per place are often unrelated or even contradictory. The new sets are three parallel hooks of the same length and shape.
